_notes: What UQM 0.8.0's own starbase screens draw, recorded by running its DoStarBase, DoOutfit and DoShipyard (with sis.c, menu.c, border.c and util.c's drawing) with each drawing call recorded in the screen's coordinates (tools/extract/golden/screens.c), on a clock of the program's own; the frames counted from the official content package (SHA-256 77d75ac25e6fb755a33c4ba3b38a7b7bc41fcbc02896891b0cc9ac9214b72eef), the fonts by their leading.

Each scenario: as outfit.json's (the story state, prices, ship), and the steps (base:S opens the menu on entry S, outfit opens outfitting, t:N runs the screen at the clock's N with no key, the rest keys), with what each drew: ["s", resource, frame, x, y] a stamp, ["f", resource, frame, x, y, r, g, b] a filled stamp, ["r"/"o"/"c", x, y, width, height, r, g, b] a filled rectangle, an outline, the clip rectangle cleared, ["p", x, y, r, g, b] a point, ["t", font, x, y, align, count, text, r, g, b, effect] text ({gs:N} is GAME_STRING (N); effect the font effect's frame of graphics.fontgradient, or -1), each with its context's clip rectangle as x, y, width, height (UQM draws only inside it); and after each step, where the flashing highlight is (sis.c's SetFlashRect: [x, y, width, height] or null) and the colour map last set (the shipyard's power lines: a map of colortable.hangar, or -1).

The shipyard ("shipyard" opens DoShipyard as DoStarBase does, with its menu on SHIPYARD; each later step runs on_input_frame, then the screen, as DoInput does) has the flagship alone: fleet ships come with stage 4.

frames: each resource's number of frames; hangar_maps: how many colour maps colortable.hangar has; rects: each frame's GetFrameRect, [x, y, width, height] (its corner less the hot spot, and its size), read from the content.
